title: Minimum Seconds to Equalize a Circular Array
statement:
You get an array `nums` of `n` integers whose ends are joined, so index `n - 1` and index `0` are neighbours. One second consists of a single step in which every position `i` at once takes a new value chosen from three options: its own current value, the current value of its left neighbour `nums[(i - 1 + n) % n]`, or the current value of its right neighbour `nums[(i + 1) % n]`. All positions read the values from before the step.

Return the fewest seconds after which every element of `nums` holds the same value (0 if they already do).
notes:
## Intuition

Each second a value can copy itself one step to the left and one step to the right, so if every element should end as `x`, the copies of `x` simply grow outward. A run of `d - 1` non-`x` positions sitting between two copies of `x` that are `d` indices apart is filled from both sides, which takes `floor(d / 2)` seconds. So the time for `x` is decided by its widest circular gap, and the answer is the smallest such time over all values. Simulating the spread for every value works too but costs O(n²).

## Approach

1. Group indices by value in the map `positions`, so each list `indices` is sorted.
2. For each list, start `widest` with the gap that wraps around the end: `indices[0] + n - last`.
3. Compare it with every gap between consecutive indices `indices[k] - indices[k - 1]` and keep the largest.
4. The seconds for this value are `floor(widest / 2)`; keep the minimum in `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 1, 2]`, `n = 4`. Value 1 sits at `[0, 2]`: the wrap gap is `0 + 4 - 2 = 2` and the inner gap is `2`, so `widest = 2` and it needs `1` second. Value 2 sits at `[1, 3]` and also gives `1`. The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is stored once and visited once more when gaps are measured.
- Space: O(n): the map holds every index.

## Pitfalls

- Do not forget the gap that wraps past the end of the array; it is often the widest one.
- A value that appears once has a single gap of length `n`, giving `floor(n / 2)`, not `n - 1`.
- The time for a gap `d` is `floor(d / 2)`, because both neighbours fill the space at the same time.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `positions` | map from each value to the sorted list of its indices |
| `indices` | the index list of the value being examined |
| `widest` | the largest circular distance between consecutive copies of that value |
| `best` | fewest seconds found so far |
